summary: Fix-forward for the view-primitive + server-side inbox search/filter/group task. All 12 review defects + the 2 addendum SECURITY blockers were re-verified adversarially. Both security blockers are REALLY closed (verified structurally, by test, and against live PG). One latent, currently-inert migration idempotency bug found (non-blocking) — follow-up chip spawned.

evidence: src/http/records.ts:1837-1845 — resolveViewApplication view lookup now carries `AND (owner_actor IS NULL OR owner_actor = $3)`; $3 = `actor`.

`actor` is bound at the LIST handler (records.ts:1920) from extractActor(req,pool) — Keycloak mode resolves ctx.sub→employee slug via resolveActorSlugFromAuth; dev mode uses x-dev-user (the dev auth mechanism). NEVER from request body or an arbitrary header.

extractActor in records.ts and list-views.ts are byte-identical in logic → the `actor` slug used in the owner clause is exactly the slug list-views.ts writes into owner_actor on create (ownerActor = personal ? actor : null). Clause therefore matches the caller's own personal views correctly.

Attack B→A: foreign personal view id → SELECT returns 0 rows → viewRow null → `throw HttpError(404, NOT_FOUND)` (records.ts:1846-1848). Indistinguishable from genuine not-found — no existence oracle. Common views (owner_actor IS NULL) remain visible to all.

list-views.ts CRUD (GET/PATCH/DELETE/getView/listViews/listSourceViews) all owner-scoped via ownerVisibilityClause; PATCH/DELETE resolve owner FIRST and only skip configurator gate for the caller's OWN personal view — a common view still requires the configurator privilege.

Test: src/__tests__/records-view-application.test.ts defect#8 cases (owner clause present + ACTOR bound as owner param, not body; foreign view → 404). Live PG: ci/checks/db/list-view-registry.db.test.ts AC-2 (cross-tenant 404) passed.

migration 130 applied to live PG (localhost:55432): schema_migrations has '130_list_view_source_owner'; list_view.source NOT NULL DEFAULT 'records', owner_actor nullable, registry_def_id/application_id now nullable.
Old table UNIQUE constraint list_view_tenant_id_registry_def_id_name_key is GONE (0 unique constraints remain); old index list_view_one_default GONE.
New partial index list_view_name_scoped_uniq (tenant, source, COALESCE(reg_def,zero-uuid), COALESCE(owner,''), name) present; new list_view_one_default_scoped + list_view_source_owner_idx present.

Live-PG proof ci/checks/db/list-view-registry.db.test.ts 'defect #9': two DIFFERENT owners reuse same personal-view name on same reg_def → BOTH succeed; same-owner dup → 23505; AC-10 (≤1 default per scope) still 23505s. All 10 tests passed against real choros_app (NOBYPASSRLS) role.
COALESCE sentinels correctly prevent NULL-not-equal-to-self from allowing duplicate inbox/processes views.

non_blocking.finding: The ELSE fallback in the constraint-DROP DO-block compares array_agg(a.attname) (type name[]) to ARRAY['name','registry_def_id','tenant_id'] (type text[]). Postgres has no name[]=text[] operator → re-applying the file raw errors 'operator does not exist: name[] = text[]'. The migration's self-documented idempotency ('повтор безопасен') is therefore INACCURATE for the fallback.
non_blocking.why_not_blocking: Currently INERT: (1) migrations/run.mjs skips already-recorded versions so 130 never re-executes in prod/CI; (2) on the real migration graph, migration 123 declares UNIQUE(tenant_id,registry_def_id,name) inline → auto-named list_view_tenant_id_registry_def_id_name_key, so the PRIMARY IF-EXISTS path always matches on first apply and the buggy ELSE is never reached. Verified: 130 is correctly applied to live PG (old constraint dropped, scoped indexes present).
non_blocking.fix: cast array_agg(a.attname::text ...) or compare against ARRAY[...]::name[]; verify by double-applying the file via psql ON_ERROR_STOP=1.
